papers.title: Multi-Objective Optimization of Selective Laser Melting Processes for Minimizing Energy Consumption and Maximizing Product Tensile Strength
papers.abstract: As a sustainable manufacturing technology, selective laser melting (SLM) is a typical additive manufacturing (AM) method with high flexibility and material efficiency. However, SLM is intrinsically energy-intensive than conventional machining processes. By contrast, part quality, especially the tensile strength, is critical for applying SLM technology. Therefore, this study aims to minimize the process energy consumption and maximize the part tensile strength by optimizing three essential process parameters, namely laser power, scan speed, and overlap rate. First, single track and single layer experiments are applied to determine the constraints of process parameters. Then, analytical and statistical models are used to calculate energy consumption and part tensile strength. Finally, the process parameters to achieve compromised optimal solutions are located using the nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II). A case study of a waveguide part manufactured via the SLM process is employed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Results showed that both energy consumption and part tensile strength could be improved moderately using the proposed method. This study can potentially guide the process parameter selection for new material AM processes and improve the AM product quality.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注SLM工艺参数优化以降低能耗和提高拉伸强度，未涉及生物医学植入物、多孔结构、应力遮挡或骨整合等方向核心内容。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical context, no porous structure for stress shielding, no LPBF fabrication of implants, no fatigue testing, and no surface morphology or osseointegration analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少SLM能耗并提高零件拉伸强度
summary_zh.method: 采用NSGA-II多目标优化激光功率、扫描速度和搭接率
summary_zh.result: 实现了能耗与拉伸强度的折中优化
summary_zh.validation: 通过波导件实例验证了方法的有效性

summary_en.motivation: To simultaneously minimize energy consumption and maximize tensile strength in selective laser melting processes.
summary_en.method: A multi-objective optimization framework using NSGA-II is applied to optimize laser power, scan speed, and overlap rate.
summary_en.result: The proposed method yields moderate improvements in both energy efficiency and tensile strength.
summary_en.validation: A waveguide part fabricated via SLM serves as a case study to demonstrate the optimization effectiveness.
